ideas.description: Exploit: finish the early-resolution dial. The tip is E036 (9.25 true epochs, about 231 steps at batch 2000; 20/24/28/32 px at 30/10/30/30%; whitening bias detached after 20%; group-1 freeze at 75%). Change only the resolution split, from 30/10/30/30 to 40/0/30/30: the 24 px phase (about 23 steps) now runs at 20 px. The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact step counts and positions. The LR, Lookahead, whitening-detach and freeze schedules stay unchanged. The 20 px graphs (full and whitening-detached variants) are already captured in build. The 24 px graphs can be dropped from build. error_on_recompile stays on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2, and discount held-out by about 0.1 pp for the winner's curse (E038). Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 0.13–0.15 s (23 steps × about 20.4 → 14.4 ms), to about 5.17–5.20 s (−2.5%). E026 and E033 show the first 30% at 20 px is free, so the held-out mean moves between −0.15 and +0.05 pp (median about −0.03). A loss of 0.1 pp or less supports H2.3.6 and puts the early-phase rate above 1.5 s/pp. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means the 20→28 px jump is now too large, and the 24 px bridge carries accuracy.

ideas.description: Exploit: non-uniform trim. Run it on the I-40/0/30/30 successor if kept, otherwise on the E036 tip. Remove only 12 steps from the 20 px phase (231 → 219 total steps). The 28 px and 32 px phases keep their exact absolute step counts. The whitening-bias detach stays at the same absolute step (about 46). The group-1 freeze still covers the same last ~58 steps. The LR triangle and the Lookahead ramp are stretched to the new total as fractions, as in E023/E027. No new shapes, so no recapture is needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Run held-out seeds 3–12 in the same session. Keep if seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753 and held-out ≥ 0.7545.
ideas.expected: Time falls about 0.17 s (12 × about 14.4 ms), about −3.3%, to about 5.0–5.15 s depending on the base. A uniform trim of the same time costs about 0.11–0.13 pp on the epoch dial. Prediction: held-out falls 0–0.1 pp (median −0.05), which beats the dial at more than 2 s/pp and supports H4.2.5. A loss of 0.15 pp or more means low-res steps count as much as late ones, so uniform trims are the right dial.

ideas.description: Explore/exploit: staggered FreezeOut, which separates where E037's cliff came from. First read group 1's structure in the code. If, as in airbench, the pool follows group 1's first conv, that conv (24→128 on 31×31 maps) and the pool are the only full-resolution work left once the whitening is detached. On the E036 tip, put only group 1's first conv in its own Muon param group. Its LR follows the global triangle to its peak, then is annealed to 0 by 60% of steps. From 60% on, detach that conv's output (before the pool), so there is no conv1 wgrad and no pool/BN backward on the 31×31 maps. The rest of group 1 keeps E036's annealed freeze at 75%. Capture the conv1-detached variants at 28 px and 32 px in build, with error_on_recompile on. Lookahead still averages every param. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. If the code shows the pool is not right after conv1, freeze whichever layers run at 31×31 instead, and record which ones.
ideas.expected: About 34 extra steps (60–75%, mostly at 28 px) skip the 31×31 backward, at about 3–5 ms each. Time falls 0.10–0.17 s (2–3%), to about 5.15–5.2 s. Held-out moves between −0.25 and 0 pp. A loss of 0.1 pp or less means E037's −0.56 pp came from freezing the deeper group-1 convs, not the full-resolution conv; that supports staggering, and the next step tests conv1 at 50%. A loss of 0.25 pp or more means the first conv itself must adapt through the 28→32 px switch.

ideas.description: Freeze-dose test of W5's crux: is E037's cliff caused by freezing before the 28→32 px switch? On the E036 tip, move only the group-1 freeze from 75% to 70% of steps, which is exactly the start of the 32 px phase. The group-1 LR is annealed to 0 by 70% instead of 75%. The truncated 32 px step variant already exists, so no new shapes are needed; error_on_recompile stays on. Steps, resolution phases, LR, Lookahead and the whitening detach are unchanged. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep if held-out ≥ 0.7545 and seeds 0–2 ≥ 0.753.
ideas.expected: About 12 more truncated 32 px steps at about 9.5 ms each: time falls about 0.11 s (−2%), to about 5.2 s. Held-out moves between −0.3 and 0 pp. If it falls 0.1 pp or less, the stem needs no 32 px adaptation, the freeze dose was linear-safe down to 70%, and 75% was conservative. If it falls 0.25 pp or more (near E037's per-step rate), the stem must see 32 px before freezing. Then the next test moves the 32 px switch earlier together with the freeze.

ideas.description: Time-neutral booster to fund the next trim, re-scoped from the vetoed I015. Two things are different now: the tip has frozen group-1 BN in train mode, and Lookahead lerps BN buffers that were built with momentum 0.6 from different fast weights. On the E036 tip, at the end of train, after the final Lookahead copy: reset every BN layer's running stats and set momentum=None (cumulative average). Then run a no-grad, train-mode forward at 32 px over 3 batches of 2000 training images with the usual crop and flip. Restore BN momentum afterwards. Capture this forward-only train-mode graph in build on synthetic channels_last tensors, with error_on_recompile on. Eval stays a plain forward pass. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2. Keep only if held-out gains at least 0.15 pp.
ideas.expected: Time rises 0.03–0.05 s (about +0.8%; 3 forward passes at about 12 ms each). Held-out moves between −0.1 and +0.25 pp, median about +0.05. A gain of at least 0.15 pp pays for about 0.35 epoch (about 0.24 s), so the booster is net positive. A change within ±0.1 pp means Lookahead's frequent resets already keep the BN stats consistent with the averaged weights. That would close H1.3.6 and, with it, the time-neutral booster search (W3's crux).

ideas.description: Explore: an even coarser start. On the E036 tip (or the 40/0/30/30 successor if kept), run only the first 15% of steps (about 35) at 16 px instead of 20 px. Map sizes become 15/7/3/1, and the global max-pool head handles 1×1. All other phases, step counts, and the LR, Lookahead, detach and freeze schedules are unchanged. Capture the 16 px graphs in build with channels_last tensors from the training code path, with error_on_recompile on. Judge on held-out seeds 3–12 as well as seeds 0–2.
ideas.expected: If 16 px scales with pixels, about 9 ms per step vs 14.4 ms at 20 px; with the off-grid discount (E024), about 12 ms. Time falls 0.08–0.18 s (1.5–3.5%). Held-out moves −0.3 to 0 pp, median −0.1. A loss of 0.1 pp or less extends the 'early resolution is free' finding below 20 px (rate above 1.5 s/pp). A loss of 0.2 pp or more marks 20 px as the floor for 100 classes.

ideas.description: Math-identical systems cleanup of trial 0's remaining prepare overhead: about 0.07 s, i.e. 0.148 vs 0.06–0.08 s (E035). In build, make one pageable host-to-device copy of a synthetic CPU uint8 tensor with exactly the training set's shape and dtype. Allocate and free GPU buffers of the sizes prepare uses, so the caching allocator and copy path are warm, and touch the same normalization and whitening ops on that synthetic data. Use no real data. Then add per-op CUDA-event timing to prepare in an offline copy to confirm where the remainder goes before committing. Check with torch.equal that the train tensor and whitening weights are unchanged, so per-seed accuracies stay bit-identical. Record per-trial prepare time.
ideas.expected: Trial-0 prepare falls from about 0.15 to about 0.07–0.09 s, so the 3-trial mean time falls about 0.02–0.03 s (−0.4–0.5%). Per-seed accuracy is bit-identical to the base build. If the remainder only appears under the harness process and is not reproducible, record that and close H3.2.

drop.reason: 3 of 5 members forecast clear harm (median −0.35 pp held-out). At best it saves about 3% (Muon NS overhead), and the tip's discounted population margin (about 0.754 after E038's winner's curse) can't absorb the likely loss. Resolving a loss of 0.15 pp or less would also take more than one 10-seed run. Better candidates (early resolution, staggered freeze, freeze dose) target 2–3% at about zero cost. It can come back if the stem and resolution levers run out.

The tip is E036: 5.31 s, held-out 3–12 at 0.7557, fresh seeds 13–22 at 0.7538, pooled 20-seed mean 0.7547. Seeds 0–2 sit near the bar on this build. The official 40-seed margin is about 0.47 pp. Every remaining time cut therefore has to be close to free, or be paired with a booster or top-up.

The new queue targets the cheapest levers found so far:
1. **Early resolution (priority 5).** Finish the early-resolution dial: 40/0/30/30, with the 24 px bridge replaced by 20 px, for about −0.14 s.
2. **Non-uniform trim (priority 4).** Cut only 20 px steps (12 steps, about −0.17 s). This tests whether early steps are worth less than late ones (H4.2.5) against the uniform epoch dial.
3. **Freeze tests (priority 3).** Two single-factor tests pin down E037's cliff:
   - Freeze only group 1's first conv, the full-resolution layer, at 60% (staggered FreezeOut).
   - Freeze all of group 1 at 70%, the 28→32 px switch. This is W5's crux.
4. **BN-stat recalibration (priority 2).** Re-scoped from the vetoed I015 as the last untested time-neutral booster (W3's crux). It costs about 0.04 s, and a gain of at least 0.15 pp funds a trim.
5. **16 px start (priority 2).** An explore test of whether 20 px is the resolution floor for 100 classes.
6. **Prepare cleanup (priority 1).** A math-identical cleanup of trial 0's remaining prepare overhead, about −0.025 s on the mean.

Kept: I058, the profiling diagnostic. It answers W2, W3, W5 and W6's cruxes on BN and memory traffic and tells the freeze ideas where the time goes. I057, the BN fold, is still running.

Dropped: I059, Muon → SGD, because the majority forecasts harm and the tip has no margin to spend on it.
